questions.question: What is the correct formula for calculating pressure, where thrust is the force applied and area is the surface it acts on?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pressure = Thrust ÷ Area**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pressure** is defined as the physical force exerted on an object per unit area. It is the ratio of **thrust** to the **area** over which that force is distributed.
 
• The mathematical formula for **pressure** is **Pressure = Thrust / Area**. This indicates that pressure is directly proportional to the magnitude of the **thrust** and inversely proportional to the **surface area**. ***Hence, the formula Pressure = Thrust ÷ Area is correct.***
 
• **Thrust** is the total force acting **perpendicularly** on a surface. It is measured in **Newtons (N)**.
 
• If the **area** is kept constant, an increase in **thrust** will lead to an increase in **pressure**. Conversely, if the **thrust** is kept constant, decreasing the **area** will significantly increase the **pressure**.
 
• This principle explains why a **sharp needle** (small area) can easily penetrate a surface compared to a **blunt object** (large area) when the same amount of **force** is applied.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **SI Unit**: The standard unit of **pressure** is the **Pascal (Pa)**, named after the **French** scientist **Blaise Pascal**. One **Pascal** is equal to one **Newton per square meter (1 N/m²)**.
 
• **Scalar Quantity**: **Pressure** is a **scalar quantity** because it does not have a specific direction of its own, even though the **force (thrust)** acting on the surface is a **vector quantity**.
 
• **Atmospheric Pressure**: This is the pressure exerted by the weight of the **atmosphere**. At **sea level**, the standard **atmospheric pressure** is approximately **101,325 Pa** or **1 atm**.
 
• **Applications in Daily Life**:
 
 
• **School Bags**: They are provided with **broad straps** to increase the **surface area**, thereby reducing the **pressure** on the shoulders of the student.
 
• **Tools**: Cutting tools like **knives** and **axes** have very **thin edges** to reduce the **area** and maximize the **pressure**, allowing them to cut through materials easily.
 
• **Foundations**: The **foundations** of high-rise **buildings** are made **wide** to distribute the heavy weight (thrust) over a larger **area**, preventing the building from sinking into the ground.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Fluid Pressure**: In **liquids** and **gases**, pressure acts in all directions. The **pressure** in a liquid increases with **depth** due to the weight of the liquid column above it. The formula for fluid pressure is **P = h × d × g**, where **h** is height, **d** is density, and **g** is acceleration due to gravity.
 
• **Conversion Units**: Apart from **Pascal**, other common units for **pressure** include **bar**, **torr**, and **pounds per square inch (psi)**. For example, **1 bar** is equal to **100,000 Pa**.
 
• **Relationship Summary**:
 
 
• Higher **Thrust** + Same **Area** = Higher **Pressure**.
 
• Same **Thrust** + Smaller **Area** = Higher **Pressure**.
 
• Same **Thrust** + Larger **Area** = Lower **Pressure**.

questions.question: A particle accelerates uniformly at 2 m/s² . Its velocity changes from 5 m/s to 15 m/s . How long does this take?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5 s**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The motion of the particle is a case of **uniformly accelerated motion** in a straight line, where the rate of change of **velocity** remains constant over **time**.
 
• The **initial velocity (u)** of the particle is given as **5 m/s**, which is its speed at the start of the measured interval.
 
• The **final velocity (v)** reached by the particle is **15 m/s**, indicating an increase in speed due to **acceleration**.
 
• The **uniform acceleration (a)** is specified as **2 m/s²**. This value represents that the particle's velocity increases by **2 meters per second** for every **one second** of motion.
 
• To determine the **time (t)** taken for this change, we use the first **equation of motion**: **v = u + at**. By substituting the known values into the equation, we get **15 = 5 + (2 × t)**.
 
• Solving for **t** involves subtracting the **initial velocity** from the **final velocity** (**15 - 5 = 10**) and then dividing by the **acceleration** (**10 / 2**), resulting in **5 seconds**. ***Hence, the correct option is 5 s.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Equations of Motion:** These equations, often attributed to the work of **Sir Isaac Newton** and **Galileo**, describe the relationship between **displacement (s)**, **velocity (v and u)**, **acceleration (a)**, and **time (t)**.
 
 
• **First Equation:** **v = u + at** (defines the velocity-time relationship).
 
• **Second Equation:** **s = ut + 1/2 at²** (defines the displacement-time relationship).
 
• **Third Equation:** **v² = u² + 2as** (defines the velocity-displacement relationship).
 
 
 
• **Uniform Acceleration:** This occurs when an object's **velocity** changes at a constant rate. In a **velocity-time graph**, **uniform acceleration** is represented by a **straight line**, and the **slope** of this line gives the **numerical value** of the **acceleration**.
 
• **SI Units:** In the **International System of Units**, **velocity** is measured in **m/s** (meters per second), **acceleration** in **m/s²** (meters per second squared), and **time** in **s** (seconds).
 
• **Vector Nature:** Both **velocity** and **acceleration** are **vector quantities**, meaning they possess both **magnitude** and **direction**. If the **acceleration** is in the opposite direction of the **velocity**, it is called **retardation** or **deceleration**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Displacement Calculation:** Using the **time** calculated (**5 s**), the **displacement** of the particle during this interval can also be found using the second equation of motion: **s = (5 × 5) + 0.5 × 2 × (5²) = 25 + 25 = 50 meters**.
 
• **Average Velocity:** For **uniformly accelerated motion**, the **average velocity** can be calculated as **(u + v) / 2**. In this case, **(5 + 15) / 2 = 10 m/s**. Multiplying this by the **time** (**10 m/s × 5 s**) also gives the **displacement** of **50 meters**.
 
• **Historical Context:** The study of **kinematics** was revolutionized in the **17th century**. Understanding these basic principles is essential for **engineering**, **astrophysics**, and **mechanical design** applications.

questions.question: Which of the following properties of 'suspension' is INCORRECT?

options.text: Particles of suspension do not scatter a beam of light.
Particles of suspension are visible to the naked eye.
Particles of suspension can be separated from the mixtures by the process of filtration.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Particles of suspension do not scatter a beam of light**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **suspension** is defined as a **heterogeneous mixture** in which the **solute particles** do not dissolve but remain suspended throughout the bulk of the medium. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• The particles of a **suspension** are quite large, typically with a **diameter greater than 1000 nanometers** (or **1 micrometer**). Due to this size, the particles are **visible to the naked eye** without the aid of a microscope. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• Particles of a **suspension scatter a beam of light** passing through it, making the **path of light visible**. This phenomenon is known as the **Tyndall Effect**. Therefore, the claim that they do not scatter light is factually **incorrect**. It is important to note that if the suspension is left to stand and the particles settle, the mixture will no longer scatter light. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• Due to their relatively large size, the particles of a **suspension** can be easily **separated from the mixture** by the physical process of **filtration**. When passed through a **filter paper**, the solid particles are trapped as **residue** while the liquid passes through. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• A **suspension** is inherently **unstable**. If left undisturbed, the particles will eventually **settle down** at the bottom of the container due to the force of **gravity**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Mixtures based on Particle Size**:
 
 
• **True Solution**: A **homogeneous mixture** where the particle size is less than **1 nanometer** (10⁻⁹ m). These particles do not scatter light and cannot be separated by **filtration**. An example is **salt dissolved in water**.
 
• **Colloid**: A **heterogeneous mixture** (though often appearing homogeneous) with particle sizes between **1 nm and 1000 nm**. They show the **Tyndall Effect** but the particles do not settle down. Examples include **milk**, **fog**, and **blood**.
 
 
 
• **Physical State of Suspension**: In a typical **suspension**, the **dispersed phase** is a solid, while the **dispersion medium** can be a liquid or a gas.
 
• **Common Examples**: Some well-known examples of **suspensions** include **chalk powder in water**, **muddy water**, **flour in water**, and **Milk of Magnesia** (Magnesium hydroxide).
 
• **Settling and Optical Properties**: When the particles in a **suspension** settle (a process called **sedimentation**), the mixture loses its ability to scatter light because the large particles are no longer distributed throughout the medium to intercept the light beam.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Tyndall Effect**: Named after the scientist **John Tyndall**, who first studied it in **1869**. It is a critical test to distinguish between a **true solution** and a **colloid** or **suspension**.
 
• **Separation Methods**: While **filtration** works for **suspensions**, **colloids** require more specialized techniques like **centrifugation** because their particles pass through standard filter papers.
 
• **Stability Comparison**: **True solutions** are the most stable, followed by **colloids**, while **suspensions** are the least stable mixtures as they undergo **phase separation** over time.

questions.question: What happens to the sound when the source vibrates faster?

options.text: The frequency and pitch become higher.
The pitch stays the same, but frequency decreases.
The sound stops producing compressions and rarefactions.

__
 
• The **frequency** of a sound wave is directly determined by the rate at which the source of the sound **vibrates**. Frequency is defined as the **number of oscillations or vibrations** per unit of **time**.
 
• When a source **vibrates faster**, the number of vibrations per **second** increases, which directly leads to a **higher frequency**.
 
• **Pitch** is the human brain's perception of the frequency of sound. There is a direct proportional relationship between frequency and pitch: as the **frequency increases**, the **pitch** of the sound also **increases**, making the sound shriller. *Hence, the statement that the frequency and pitch become higher is correct.*
 
• Conversely, if the source **vibrates slower**, the **frequency decreases**, and the resulting **pitch is lower**, making the sound appear deeper or more "grave."
 
• It is important to note that the **speed of sound** in a specific medium at a constant temperature remains relatively **constant**, regardless of the change in frequency or pitch.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Frequency and its Unit**: The **SI unit** of frequency is the **Hertz (Hz)**, named in honor of the physicist **Heinrich Rudolf Hertz**. **One Hertz** represents **one vibration per second**.
 
• **Nature of Sound Waves**: Sound travels as a **longitudinal mechanical wave**. It moves through a medium by creating regions of high pressure called **compressions** and regions of low pressure called **rarefactions**. As long as the source vibrates, these regions are produced; they do not stop just because the vibration speed changes.
 
• **Amplitude vs. Frequency**: While **frequency** determines **pitch**, the **amplitude** of the vibration determines the **loudness** or intensity of the sound. A higher amplitude results in a **louder sound**, whereas a higher frequency results in a **higher pitch**.
 
• **Human Auditory Range**: The typical range of hearing for a healthy **human ear** is between **20 Hz and 20,000 Hz**. Frequencies below **20 Hz** are termed **infrasonic**, and frequencies above **20,000 Hz (20 kHz)** are termed **ultrasonic**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Wavelength Relationship**: According to the wave equation (**Velocity = Frequency × Wavelength**), if the velocity is constant, an **increase in frequency** (faster vibration) results in a **decrease in wavelength**.
 
• **Examples in Nature**: A **bird** produces a **high-pitched sound** because its vocal cords vibrate at a **high frequency**, whereas a **lion's roar** is **low-pitched** because the vibrations occur at a **lower frequency**, even though the roar is much **louder** due to higher **amplitude**.
 
• **Factors Affecting Pitch**: In musical instruments like a **guitar**, tightening the string increases the tension, causing it to **vibrate faster** when plucked, thereby producing a **higher pitch**. Similarly, in wind instruments like a **flute**, shortening the air column increases the **frequency** of vibration.

questions.question: Which of the following situations clearly illustrates Newton’s third law, where action and reaction forces act on two different objects and are equal and opposite?

options.text: A stone resting on the ground.
A car accelerating due to engine power.
A sailor pushes the boat backward while jumping forward, and the boat pushes him forward.
A book kept on a table remains at rest.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A sailor pushes the boat backward while jumping forward, and the boat pushes him forward**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Newton’s Third Law of Motion**, famously articulated by **Sir Isaac Newton** in **1687**, states that for every **action**, there is an equal and opposite **reaction**.
 
• In the instance of a **sailor jumping out of a boat**, the sailor exerts a force on the boat to move away from it. This force is directed **backward** and is considered the **action**.
 
• According to the law, the boat simultaneously exerts an **equal and opposite force** on the sailor directed **forward**, which is the **reaction**. This reaction force is what actually propels the sailor forward onto the dock or land. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• A critical feature illustrated here is that the **action and reaction forces** act on **two different objects** (the sailor and the boat). This prevents the forces from canceling each other out, resulting in the **acceleration** of both bodies in opposite directions.
 
• The movement of the boat backward as the sailor leaps forward is a classic demonstration of this **reciprocal interaction**, often referred to as the **recoil** effect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Newton’s First Law (Law of Inertia)**:
 
 
• This law states that an object will remain at **rest** or in **uniform motion** unless acted upon by an **external unbalanced force**.
 
• A **stone resting on the ground** or a **book kept on a table** remains stationary because the **gravitational force** pulling it down is perfectly balanced by the **normal force** pushing up from the surface. ***Hence, statements 1 and 4 primarily illustrate equilibrium and the First Law.***
 
 
 
• **Newton’s Second Law (Law of Acceleration)**:
 
 
• This law defines the relationship between **force, mass, and acceleration**, expressed by the formula **Force = mass x acceleration**.
 
• A **car accelerating** due to engine power demonstrates how the application of a net force results in a change in **velocity** over **time**. ***Hence, statement 2 is an application of the Second Law.***
 
 
 
• **Universal Applications of the Third Law**:
 
 
• **Rocket Propulsion**: The rocket engine expels **exhaust gases** downward (action), and the gases push the rocket **upward** (reaction).
 
• **Swimming**: A swimmer pushes the **water backward** with their hands (action), and the water pushes the **swimmer forward** (reaction).
 
• **Walking**: When we walk, our feet push **backward against the ground** (action), and the ground pushes our **feet forward** (reaction), allowing movement.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Simultaneity**: It is important to note that the **action and reaction** occur at the exact same **instant**; there is no **time lag** between them.
 
• **Magnitude and Direction**: The forces are **mathematically equal** in **magnitude** but **exactly 180 degrees opposite** in **direction**.
 
• **Different Masses**: Even though the forces are equal, the resulting **accelerations** can be very different. For example, if a **stone** falls toward the **Earth**, the stone pulls the Earth up with the same force the Earth pulls the stone down, but the Earth's **immense mass** makes its acceleration undetectable.
 
• **Nature of Forces**: Action-reaction pairs are always of the **same type**. If the action is a **magnetic force**, the reaction must also be a magnetic force.

Select the option that is true regarding the following two statements labelled Assertion (A) and Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Vegetative propagation helps grow plants that do not produce seeds.
Reason (R): It uses flowers to grow new plants.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Assertion (A)**: **Vegetative propagation** is a type of **asexual reproduction** where new plants are produced from the **vegetative parts** of the parent plant, such as **roots**, **stems**, and **leaves**. It is an essential method for cultivating plants that have lost the ability to produce **seeds** or produce non-viable seeds, such as **banana**, **seedless grapes**, **rose**, **jasmine**, and **sugarcane**. ***Hence, Assertion (A) is correct.***
 
• **Reason (R)**: In the process of vegetative propagation, new plants are derived from **non-reproductive parts**. **Flowers**, on the other hand, are the **reproductive organs** of a plant involved in **sexual reproduction**, which leads to the formation of **fruits** and **seeds**. Since vegetative propagation specifically bypasses the use of flowers and seeds to create offspring, the claim that it uses flowers is factually incorrect. ***Hence, Reason (R) is false.***
 
• Vegetative propagation ensures that the **daughter plants** are **genetically identical** to the parent plant, effectively creating **clones**. This is beneficial for maintaining desirable traits in **agriculture** and **horticulture**.
 
• Plants grown through this method often **flower** and **bear fruits** much **faster** than those grown from **seeds**, providing a significant time advantage for **farmers**.
 
• ***Therefore, while the assertion correctly identifies a primary use of vegetative propagation, the reason provided is incorrect because flowers are the site of sexual reproduction, not vegetative propagation.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Natural Methods of Vegetative Propagation**:
 
 
• **Roots**: New plants emerge from **adventitious buds** on roots, as seen in **sweet potato** and **dahlia**.
 
• **Stems**: **Tubers** (like **potato** with "eyes"), **rhizomes** (like **ginger** and **turmeric**), and **runners** (like **strawberry**) are common examples of stem-based propagation.
 
• **Leaves**: Certain plants like **Bryophyllum** produce **buds** along the margins of their **leaves**. When these leaves fall on **moist soil**, the buds develop into independent new plants.
 
 
 
• **Artificial Methods of Vegetative Propagation**:
 
 
• **Cutting**: A part of the **stem** is cut and buried in the soil to grow a new plant, commonly used for **money plants** and **roses**.
 
• **Grafting**: Joining a **scion** (part of one plant) with a **stock** (rooted part of another plant) so they grow as a single plant, widely used in **mango** and **apple** cultivation.
 
• **Layering**: A **branch** is bent to the ground and covered with soil until it develops **roots**, used for **jasmine** and **lemon**.
 
• **Tissue Culture**: A modern **biotechnological** technique where **cells** or **tissues** are grown in a **nutrient medium** under **sterile conditions** to produce **plantlets**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Advantages**: It allows for the **rapid multiplication** of plants. It is the only way to multiply **seedless varieties**. It preserves the **genetic purity** (homozygosity) of a **cultivar**.
 
• **Disadvantages**: Because all offspring are **clones**, there is no **genetic variation**. This makes the entire **population** susceptible to the same **diseases** or **environmental changes**, which could lead to total **crop failure**.
 
• **Evolutionary Context**: Unlike **sexual reproduction**, which involves the **fusion of gametes** and promotes **evolution** through **variation**, vegetative propagation is a conservative process focused on **stability**.

questions.question: The amount of solute dissolved in a particular solvent is defined in terms of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**concentration**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **concentration** of a solution is defined as the amount of **solute** present in a given quantity of **solvent** or **solution**. It describes the ratio of the components in a mixture.
 
• A **solute** is the substance that is being dissolved (usually present in a **smaller amount**), while a **solvent** is the medium in which the solute is dissolved (usually present in a **larger amount**).
 
• **Concentration** can be expressed qualitatively as **dilute** (low amount of solute) or **concentrated** (high amount of solute).
 
• Quantitatively, it is measured using various units such as **Molarity**, **Molality**, **Normality**, and **Mole Fraction** to provide precise data for chemical reactions.
 
• A **saturated solution** is one in which no more solute can be dissolved at a specific **temperature** and **pressure**, representing the maximum concentration possible under those conditions. ***Hence, the correct answer is concentration.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Common Units of Concentration:**
 
 
• **Molarity (M)**: It is the number of **moles of solute** dissolved in **one liter (1L)** of solution. It is the most common unit used in laboratories.
 
• **Molality (m)**: It is the number of **moles of solute** per **kilogram (1kg)** of solvent. This unit is preferred when studying properties involving **temperature changes** because mass does not change with temperature.
 
• **Mass Percentage (% w/w)**: This represents the mass of the solute in **100 grams** of the total solution.
 
• **Parts Per Million (ppm)**: Used for extremely **dilute solutions**, such as measuring pollutants in water or air, representing **one part** of solute in **one million parts** of the solution.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Concentration:**
 
 
• **Solubility**: The maximum amount of solute that can dissolve in a solvent at a **specific temperature**.

questions.question: The resistance of a wire is 1 Omega . If it is cut into two equal parts, the resistance of each part will be:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **resistance** of a conductor is defined as the property by which it opposes the flow of **electric current** through it. It is mathematically expressed by the formula **R = ρ (L / A)**, where **R** is the resistance, **ρ (rho)** is the **electrical resistivity**, **L** is the **length**, and **A** is the **cross-sectional area**.
 
• From the formula, it is evident that the **resistance** of a wire is **directly proportional** to its **length** (**R ∝ L**). This means that if the length of the wire is increased, the resistance increases, and if the length is decreased, the resistance decreases accordingly. ***Hence, the reduction in length directly impacts the resistance value.***
 
• In this specific case, a wire with an initial resistance of **1 Ω** is cut into **two equal parts**. This implies that the new **length** of each part becomes **half** of the original length (**L' = L / 2**).
 
• Since the wire is only cut and not stretched or compressed, the **cross-sectional area (A)** and the **material (resistivity ρ)** remain **constant** for each of the two parts.
 
• By substituting the new length into the resistance formula: **R' = ρ ( (L/2) / A ) = 1/2 [ ρ (L / A) ] = R / 2**. Given the original resistance **R = 1 Ω**, the new resistance **R'** for each part is **1 / 2 = 0.5 Ω**. ***Hence, the correct answer is 0.5 Ω.***

• **Length (L)**: As discussed, **resistance** increases with **length**. This is because **electrons** encounter more **collisions** with **atoms** while traveling a longer path.
 
• **Area of Cross-section (A)**: **Resistance** is **inversely proportional** to the **area** (**R ∝ 1/A**). A **thicker wire** offers less resistance compared to a **thinner wire** because there is more space for the **electrons** to flow.
 
• **Material**: Different materials have different **resistivities (ρ)**. Conductors like **Copper** and **Aluminum** have low resistivity, while insulators like **Glass** or **Rubber** have extremely high resistivity.
 
• **Temperature**: For **metallic conductors**, resistance typically **increases** with an increase in **temperature** due to increased thermal agitation of the atoms.
 
 
 
• **Ohm’s Law:**
 
 
• Proposed by **Georg Simon Ohm** in **1827**, it states that the **current (I)** flowing through a conductor is **directly proportional** to the **potential difference (V)** across its ends, provided physical conditions like **temperature** remain constant (**V = IR**).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Stretching vs. Cutting:** If a wire is **stretched** to double its length, its **volume** remains constant, causing the **area** to decrease. In such a case, the **resistance** increases by **four times** (**n²**). However, in **cutting**, the **area** remains the **same**, so the resistance changes **linearly** with **length**.

questions.question: Which reaction best supports the Law of Conservation of Mass?

options.text: Mixing of vinegar and baking soda in a sealed container
Evaporation of alcohol in open air
Burning of paper in open air

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mixing of vinegar and baking soda in a sealed container**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Law of Conservation of Mass** states that **mass** in an isolated system is neither **created** nor **destroyed** by **chemical reactions** or **physical transformations**. This means the **mass of the products** must equal the **mass of the reactants**.
 
• **Mixing of vinegar and baking soda in a sealed container** is the best example because a **sealed container** prevents any **gaseous products** (like **carbon dioxide**) from escaping into the **atmosphere**. By weighing the container before and after the reaction, the **total mass** remains constant, directly proving the law. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• **Heating iron in open air** involves the iron reacting with **oxygen** from the surrounding **atmosphere** to form **iron oxide** (rust). In an **open system**, the final product will weigh more than the initial iron because the mass of the **absorbed oxygen** is not factored into the starting weight by a casual observer. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Evaporation of alcohol in open air** is a **physical change** where the **liquid alcohol** turns into **vapor**. Since it happens in **open air**, the **alcohol molecules** disperse into the **environment**, leading to a **decrease** in the measurable mass of the remaining liquid. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Burning of paper in open air** results in the production of **ash**, **carbon dioxide**, and **water vapor**. In an **open system**, the **gases** escape, leaving only the **ash** behind, which weighs significantly **less** than the original paper, making it appear as though mass was lost. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Antoine Lavoisier**: A **French chemist** often referred to as the **Father of Modern Chemistry**, he formulated the **Law of Conservation of Mass** in **1789**. His meticulous **quantitative experiments** with **combustion** and **oxidation** laid the foundation for modern **stoichiometry**.
 
• **Open vs. Closed Systems**: An **open system** can exchange both **energy** and **matter** with its surroundings, while a **closed system** can exchange **energy** but not **matter**. To experimentally verify the **Law of Conservation of Mass**, a **closed system** (like a **sealed flask** or **container**) is essential, especially when **gases** are involved as **reactants** or **products**.
 
• **The Vinegar and Baking Soda Reaction**: This is an **acid-base reaction**. The **acetic acid** (vinegar) reacts with **sodium bicarbonate** (baking soda) to produce **sodium acetate**, **water**, and **carbon dioxide gas**. The chemical equation is: **CH3COOH + NaHCO3 -> CH3COONa + H2O + CO2**.
 
• **Significance in Stoichiometry**: This law is fundamental for **balancing chemical equations**. It ensures that the **number of atoms** of each **element** is the **same** on both the **reactant** and **product** sides of the equation, reflecting that **atoms** are merely **rearranged**, not created or lost.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mass-Energy Equivalence**: While the **Law of Conservation of Mass** holds true for **chemical reactions**, in **nuclear reactions**, mass can be converted into **energy** according to **Albert Einstein's** equation **E = mc²**. In such cases, the **combined conservation** of **mass-energy** is observed.
 
• **Practical Application**: This law is used daily in **industrial processes**, **cooking**, and **environmental science** to calculate **yields** and track **pollutants**. For example, in **water treatment**, the amount of **chemicals** added must be balanced against the **impurities** removed to ensure **mass balance**.
 
• **Historical Context**: Before **Lavoisier**, the **Phlogiston theory** was widely accepted, which suggested that **mass** was lost during **combustion** because a substance called "**phlogiston**" was released. Lavoisier's **accurate weighing** of **mercury oxide** reactions eventually **disproved** this theory.
</ul

questions.question: Food web consists of different types of _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**food chains**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **food web** is a complex, **interconnected network of food chains** that represents the feeding relationships within an ecological community.
 
• While a **food chain** follows a single, **linear path** of energy flow (e.g., grass → grasshopper → frog → snake), a **food web** shows how various food chains overlap and connect. ***Hence, the statement that a food web consists of different food chains is correct.***
 
• In a **food web**, an organism can occupy **multiple trophic levels** simultaneously. For instance, an **omnivore** like a bear may eat berries (acting as a primary consumer) and fish (acting as a secondary or tertiary consumer).
 
• The **food web** provides a more **realistic model** of energy flow in an **ecosystem** because most organisms consume more than one type of prey and are, in turn, preyed upon by multiple predators.
 
• The structure of a **food web** ensures **ecosystem stability**; if one species is removed, the multiple pathways of the web allow the system to maintain its balance by shifting energy flow to other **food chains**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Trophic Levels:**
 
 
• These are the functional positions of organisms within a **food chain** or **web**. 
 
• The **first trophic level** consists of **producers** (autotrophs like plants and algae). 
 
• The **second level** includes **herbivores** (primary consumers), followed by **carnivores** and **omnivores** at higher levels.
 
 
 
• **The 10% Rule:**
 
 
• Proposed by **Raymond Lindeman** in **1942**, this ecological law states that only about **10% of the energy** is transferred from one **trophic level** to the next. 
 
• The remaining **90%** is lost as **heat** during metabolic processes or used for growth and respiration.
 
 
 
• **Decomposers and Detritivores:**
 
 
• Organisms like **fungi**, **bacteria**, and **earthworms** play a vital role in the **food web** by breaking down dead organic matter. 
 
• They recycle essential **nutrients** back into the soil, making them available again for **producers**.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Pyramids:**
 
 
• These are graphical representations designed to show the **biomass**, **energy**, or **number of organisms** at each trophic level. 
 
• In most healthy **ecosystems**, the **pyramid of energy** is always **upright**, meaning energy decreases as you move up the levels.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Bioaccumulation and Biomagnification:** In a **food web**, certain **pollutants** (like **mercury** or **DDT**) do not break down and instead increase in concentration as they move up to higher **trophic levels**, often harming **apex predators**.
 
• **Keystone Species:** Some species have a **disproportionately large effect** on their **food web**. If a **keystone species** (like a wolf or sea otter) is removed, the entire **ecosystem** structure can collapse or change drastically.
 
• **Types of Food Chains:** There are two main types: the **grazing food chain** (starts with green plants) and the **detritus food chain** (starts with dead organic matter). Both intermingle to form the **food web**.

 P : 17 :: 42 : 6 
 × 7

questions.question: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹4,000 at 6% per annum rate of interest for the period from 22 February 2024 to 23 April 2024.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a leap year (2024), total days = 366.

Days from 22 Feb to 23 Apr = 7 (Feb) + 31 (Mar) + 23 (Apr) = 61 days.

Simple Interest = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

SI = (4000 × 6 × 61) ÷ (100 × 366)

SI = 240 × (1 ÷ 6) = 40

**∴ The correct answer is ₹40.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Rate (R) = 6% per annum

Time period = 22 February 2024 to 23 April 2024

**Formula Used:**

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
• 
 22 Feb 2024 P = ₹4000 23 Apr 2024 SI = ₹40 Rate = 6% p.a. Time = 61 days 2024 is a Leap Year = 366 days 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Year 2024 is exactly divisible by 4, so it is a leap year with 366 days.

⇒ February in a leap year has 29 days.

⇒ Number of days in February (excluding 22nd) = 29 − 22 = 7 days.

⇒ Number of days in March = 31 days.

⇒ Number of days in April (up to 23rd) = 23 days.

⇒ Total Time (T) = 7 + 31 + 23 = 61 days.

⇒ Time converted into years = 61 ÷ 366 = 1 ÷ 6 year.

⇒ SI = (4000 × 6 × 1) ÷ (100 × 6)

⇒ SI = 24000 ÷ 600 = 40

**∴ The correct answer is ₹40.**

Counting Days for Interest

Generally, the day the money is deposited is not counted, but the day it is withdrawn is included in the total interest calculation.

Leap Year Calculation

A year is considered a leap year if it is perfectly divisible by 4 (and by 400 if it is a century year). Simple Interest calculations must use 366 days as the base denominator for a leap year unless explicitly stated otherwise.

Simple vs Compound Interest

In Simple Interest, the principal amount remains constant throughout the entire period. In Compound Interest, interest gets periodically added to the principal and earns further interest.

questions.question: Where will India’s first electronic waste (e‑waste) eco‑park be established by the Delhi government as a model for sustainable urban development?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Holambi Kalan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Delhi Government** approved the development of India’s first electronic waste (e-waste) eco-park at **Holambi Kalan** in **North West Delhi**.
 
• Spanning across approximately **21 acres**, the facility is designed to be a state-of-the-art hub for the **scientific disposal** and **recycling** of electronic waste.
 
• The park aims to address the growing issue of e-waste by integrating the **informal sector** into a formal, regulated framework, ensuring safe handling of hazardous materials.
 
• It functions as an integrated center where **dismantling, refurbishing, and material recovery** take place under one roof, serving as a model for sustainable urban development in **India**.
 
• This initiative was officially announced and approved by the **Delhi Cabinet** in **February 2022** to mitigate the environmental risks posed by the massive amount of e-waste generated in the national capital.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Understanding E-Waste:**
 
 
• Electronic waste includes discarded **computers, smartphones, televisions, refrigerators,** and **circuit boards** that have reached the end of their useful life.
 
• India is currently the **third-largest producer** of e-waste in the world, following **China** and the **USA**.
 
• Delhi alone produces roughly **2 lakh tonnes** of e-waste annually, which accounts for nearly **9.5%** of the total e-waste generated in the country.
 
 
 
• **Components of the Eco-Park:**
 
 
• The **Holambi Kalan** facility will house specialized units for **pre-processing, metal extraction,** and **refining**.
 
• It will focus on recovering valuable resources such as **gold, silver, copper,** and **aluminum** from electronic components, which otherwise end up in landfills.
 
• The park will also include **training centers** for workers to learn modern and safe recycling techniques.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Environmental and Health Safety:**
 
 
• E-waste contains toxic substances like **lead, mercury, cadmium,** and **brominated flame retardants** which can cause severe health issues and soil contamination if not handled properly.
 
• By moving recycling to a regulated **eco-park**, the government ensures that these toxins do not leach into the **groundwater** or pollute the **atmosphere** during processing.
 
 
 
• **Regulatory Framework:**
 
 
• The management of such waste is governed by the **E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2016**, and the revised **2022 rules**, which emphasize **Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR)**.
 
• Under **EPR**, manufacturers and producers are held accountable for the end-of-life management of the electronic products they place on the market.
 
• The **Delhi State Pollution Control Committee (DPCC)** plays a crucial role in monitoring the standards and operations within such environmental projects.

questions.question: In June 2025, which of the following organizations published the Global Economic Prospects (GEP) report, a flagship publication providing analysis of global economic trends, forecasts, and risks?

__
 
• The **Global Economic Prospects (GEP)** is a **flagship report** issued by the **World Bank Group** that examines **global economic developments** and prospects, with a special focus on **emerging market and developing economies (EMDEs)**.
 
• It is published **twice a year**, typically in **January** and **June**. The report issued in **June 2025** continues the tradition of providing **comprehensive forecasts** for **global growth**, **inflation**, and **trade**.
 
• The **GEP** serves as a vital tool for **policymakers** and **investors** by identifying **downside risks** such as **geopolitical instability**, **high debt levels**, and **financial market volatility**.
 
• The report often includes analytical chapters on topical issues, such as the impact of **interest rate cycles**, **investment trends**, and the **economic consequences** of **climate change** on **developing nations**.
 
• By providing **data-driven insights** and **forecasts** for over **150 countries**, the **World Bank** helps guide **international development strategies** and **poverty reduction** efforts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **World Bank Group:**
 
 
• Established in **1944** at the **Bretton Woods Conference**, it is headquartered in **Washington, D.C.**, **United States**.
 
• It comprises **five institutions**, including the **International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD)** and the **International Development Association (IDA)**.
 
• Its primary goals are to **end extreme poverty** and promote **shared prosperity** by providing **loans**, **grants**, and **technical assistance** to **low and middle-income countries**.
 
 
 
• **International Monetary Fund (IMF):**
 
 
• While often confused with the World Bank, the **IMF** publishes the **World Economic Outlook (WEO)** and the **Global Financial Stability Report**.
 
• The **IMF** focuses primarily on **macroeconomic stability**, **exchange rate regimes**, and providing **temporary financial assistance** to countries facing **balance of payments** crises.
 
 
 
• **Asian Development Bank (ADB):**
 
 
• Founded in **1966** and based in **Manila**, **Philippines**, the **ADB** focuses on the **Asia-Pacific region**.
 
• Its flagship publication is the **Asian Development Outlook (ADO)**, which provides **economic analysis** and **growth projections** specifically for **Asian economies**.
 
 
 
• **World Economic Forum (WEF):**
 
 
• An **international non-governmental organization** based in **Cologny**, **Switzerland**, famous for its **annual meeting** in **Davos**.
 
• It publishes the **Global Risks Report** and the **Global Competitiveness Report**, focusing on **public-private cooperation** and **global governance**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **World Bank** also publishes the **World Development Report (WDR)**, which is an **annual guide** to the **economic, social, and environmental state** of the world today.
 
• As of **2024-2025**, the **World Bank** is led by **President Ajay Banga**, who has emphasized **climate finance** and **private sector mobilization** as key pillars of the bank's **evolution roadmap**.
 
• The **GEP** report is distinct from the **Global Financial Development Report**, another **World Bank** publication that focuses specifically on the **financial sector's** role in **development**.
</ul

questions.question: According to the World Bank's Poverty and Equity Brief Report 2025, India’s extreme poverty rate fell from 16.2% (in 2011-12) to what percentage in 2022-23?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2.3%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **World Bank's Poverty and Equity Brief Report 2025**, India has demonstrated a significant decline in extreme poverty over the last decade.
 
• The extreme poverty rate in India, measured using the international poverty line of **$2.15** per person per day (at **2017 PPP**), fell to **2.3%** in the year **2022-23**.
 
• In the **2011-12** period, the extreme poverty rate was recorded at **16.2%**, highlighting a sharp reduction in the proportion of the population living in absolute deprivation.
 
• The data used in this brief is primarily based on the **Household Consumption Expenditure Survey (HCES)** for **2022-23**, which was released by the **National Sample Survey Office (NSSO)** under the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)**.
 
• This trend indicates that India is moving closer to achieving the **Sustainable Development Goal 1** (SDG 1) of ending poverty in all its forms by **2030**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **International Poverty Line:**
 
 
• The **World Bank** updated the global extreme poverty line to **$2.15** in **September 2022**, replacing the previous **$1.90** line. This change was based on **2017 Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)** to reflect changes in the cost of living across countries.
 
 
 
• **Household Consumption Expenditure Survey (HCES) 2022-23:**
 
 
• This survey was crucial as it provided official consumption data for India after a gap of **11 years**. It used a revamped methodology, including multiple visits to households and a modernized questionnaire, to capture consumption patterns accurately.
 
 
 
• **Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI):**
 
 
• Apart from income-based poverty, **NITI Aayog** tracks **Multidimensional Poverty** in India. Their **2024** reports suggest that nearly **24.82 crore** Indians escaped multidimensional poverty between **2013-14** and **2022-23**.
 
 
 
• **Gini Index and Inequality:**
 
 
• The **World Bank** report also monitors the **Gini Index**, which measures consumption inequality. Recent data suggests that while poverty has decreased, consumption inequality in India has shown signs of stabilization, with the **Gini coefficient** in rural areas declining more noticeably than in urban areas.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Social Welfare Schemes:** Large-scale government interventions such as the **Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PM-GKAY)**, which provides free foodgrains to approximately **80 crore** beneficiaries, have played a vital role in cushioning the vulnerable population from extreme poverty, especially during the **COVID-19 pandemic**.
 
• **Purchasing Power Parity (PPP):** The calculations utilize **2017 PPP** dollars, which is a spatial price index that allows for the comparison of the real value of currencies across different countries, neutralizing the effect of price level differences.
 
• **Regional Variations:** While the national average stands at **2.3%**, the **World Bank** notes that poverty reduction has been widespread, though specific states in the **BIMARU** region continue to require targeted policy interventions to sustain these gains.
</ul

questions.question: Which organisation confirmed strong economic growth in India’s industrial and services sectors in May 2025, despite unemployment challenges?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, in its economic assessment for **May 2025**, confirmed that India’s **industrial** and **services sectors** continue to lead the nation's **economic growth**.
 
• The **central bank** highlighted that the **Services sector** remained the primary engine of the **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)**, bolstered by strong domestic demand and **export of services**.
 
• The **Industrial sector** showed significant resilience, particularly in **Manufacturing** and **Construction**, supported by the government’s **Capital Expenditure (CAPEX)** initiatives and the **Production Linked Incentive (PLI)** schemes.
 
• Despite the positive trajectory in production and output, the **RBI** raised concerns regarding **unemployment challenges**, noting that the growth has not yet fully translated into proportionate **job creation** across all demographics.
 
• The **RBI** uses high-frequency indicators such as the **Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI)** and **GST collections** to validate these growth trends in the **May 2025** report.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI):**
 
 
• Established on **April 1, 1935**, under the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**, following the recommendations of the **Hilton Young Commission**.
 
• It was **nationalized** on **January 1, 1949**, and serves as the **Central Bank** of India, regulating the **monetary policy** and the **banking system**.
 
• The **Governor of RBI** (currently **Shaktikanta Das** as of recent years) leads the **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)**, which meets **bi-monthly** to decide on interest rates like the **Repo Rate**.
 
 
 
• **Industrial and Services Sector Metrics:**
 
 
• **Index of Industrial Production (IIP):** An index that details the growth of various sectors in the economy such as **Mining**, **Manufacturing**, and **Electricity**.
 
• **PMI (Purchasing Managers' Index):** An indicator of the economic health of the manufacturing and service sectors; a reading above **50** indicates **expansion**.
 
• The **Services Sector** in India contributes more than **50%** to the **Gross Value Added (GVA)**, making it the most dominant part of the economy.
 
 
 
• **Unemployment and Labor Trends:**
 
 
• **Unemployment** is often tracked via the **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)** conducted by the **National Statistical Office (NSO)** under the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation**.
 
• "Jobless growth" is a condition where the economy grows without a corresponding increase in **employment opportunities**, a phenomenon the **RBI** monitors to ensure **financial stability**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of NITI Aayog:** While **NITI Aayog** (National Institution for Transforming India) serves as the **policy think-tank** of the government, the **RBI** is the statutory body responsible for the **macroeconomic data** and **inflation control**.
 
• **Financial Stability Report (FSR):** This is a **bi-annual** report released by the **RBI** that assesses the resilience of India's **financial sector** and identifies risks to **economic growth**.
 
• **Growth vs. Development:** The **RBI** often distinguishes between **numerical growth** (GDP) and **inclusive development** (employment and equity), emphasizing that sustainable growth requires a **robust labor market**.
 
• **Foreign Exchange Reserves:** In **2025**, the **RBI** continues to manage India’s **Forex Reserves** to protect the **Indian Rupee (INR)** against **global volatility**.

• In **September 2025**, the female cheetah named **Dheera** was released into the **Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary** in **Madhya Pradesh** as part of the ongoing **Project Cheetah**.

• **Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary** was specifically prepared with a **predator-proof enclosure** spanning approximately **64 square kilometers** to ensure the safety and successful breeding of the translocated felines.
 
• The introduction of **Dheera** and other cheetahs to this sanctuary aims to strengthen **breeding efforts** and provide a diverse habitat consisting of **open grasslands** and dry deciduous forests, which are ideal for the species.
 
• This translocation is overseen by the **National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA)** in collaboration with international experts from **Namibia** and **South Africa**.

• **Project Cheetah:**
 
 
• Launched in **September 2022**, this is the world’s first **intercontinental large wild carnivore translocation** project.
 
• The project aims to reintroduce the **Asiatic Cheetah** (now extinct in India) by using its close relative, the **African Cheetah**.
 
• The first batch of **8 cheetahs** was brought from **Namibia**, followed by **12 cheetahs** from **South Africa** in **February 2023**.
 
 
 
• **Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary:**
 
 
• It is located on the northern boundary of **Mandsaur** and **Neemuch** districts in **Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• The sanctuary is bisected by the **Chambal River**, which provides a perennial water source for the local wildlife.
 
• It was selected as the second site for cheetah reintroduction due to its **prey base** (including Chinkara and Spotted Deer) and suitable terrain.

• **Sasha:** One of the initial Namibian cheetahs; unfortunately, she was the first to succumb to a **kidney ailment** in **March 2023**.
 
• **Jwala:** Noted for giving birth to the first litter of **cheetah cubs** born on Indian soil in over **70 years**.
 
 
 
• **Conservation Goals:**
 
 
• The long-term goal is to reach a self-sustaining population of about **35 to 40 cheetahs** across multiple sites in **Central India**.
 
• Reintroducing cheetahs helps in the **restoration of open forest** and grassland ecosystems, which supports biodiversity conservation at a larger scale.

questions.question: What type of weapon is DRDO planning to test under the DURGA-2 project?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Laser Weapon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **DURGA-2**, which stands for **Directionally Unrestricted Ray-Gun Array**, is a classified project of the **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** to develop a high-power **Laser Weapon**.
 
• The project is being spearheaded by the **Laser Science and Technology Centre (LASTEC)**, a premier laboratory based in **New Delhi** that specializes in **Directed Energy Weapons (DEWs)**.
 
• The **DURGA-2** system is designed as a **100-kilowatt**, lightweight **Directed Energy Weapon** that can be integrated into land, sea, and air-based platforms.
 
• The weapon works by emitting a highly concentrated **laser beam** to damage or destroy targets such as **Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs)**, **ballistic missiles**, and **enemy fighter jets** by melting their airframes or blinding their sensors.
 
• Unlike conventional munitions, this **Laser Weapon** provides a **low cost per shot** because it utilizes electrical energy instead of expensive physical missiles or shells.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Directed Energy Weapons (DEWs):**
 
 
• **DEWs** are systems that use concentrated **electromagnetic energy** or **atomic particles** to incapacitate or destroy enemy equipment and personnel.
 
• The primary types of **DEWs** include **High-Energy Lasers (HEL)** and **High-Power Microwaves (HPM)**.
 
• These weapons engage targets at the **speed of light**, making them effective against high-speed threats like **hypersonic missiles**.
 
 
 
• **KALI (Kilo Ampere Linear Injector):**
 
 
• Apart from **DURGA-2**, **India** is also working on **KALI**, a linear accelerator being developed by **DRDO** and the **Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC)**.
 
• **KALI** is designed to emit powerful pulses of **electrons** to destroy the electronic systems of incoming **missiles** and **aircraft**.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• Several countries are racing to deploy **Laser Weapons**, including the **United States** (with its **Laser Weapon System - LaWS**), **Russia** (with **Peresvet**), and **Israel** (with the **Iron Beam**).
 
• The **United Kingdom** recently tested its **DragonFire** laser system, demonstrating the tactical shift toward **non-kinetic warfare**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Strategic Advantages:** The **DURGA-2** provides a stealthy engagement capability as the **laser beam** is invisible to the naked eye and produces no sound during firing.
 
• **Tactical Applications:** It is particularly effective for **Short-Range Air Defence (SHORAD)**, protecting vital installations from **swarms of drones** which are difficult to intercept using traditional air defense systems.
 
• **Research and Development:** **LASTEC** has been focusing on **solid-state lasers** and **fiber lasers** to ensure the **DURGA-2** system remains compact enough for mobile military trucks and naval ships.
 
• **Power Requirements:** Achieving a **100kW** output is a significant milestone for **India**, as it provides enough thermal energy to neutralize hardened **military targets** at distances of several kilometers.
</ul

questions.question: Which milestone did Tata Lockheed Martin Aerostructures (TLMAL), a joint venture of Tata Advanced Systems (TASL) and Lockheed Martin achieve in India’s defence manufacturing in December 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Delivery of 250th C-130J tail assembly**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **December 2025**, **Tata Lockheed Martin Aerostructures (TLMAL)** achieved a significant milestone in **India's** defense manufacturing sector by delivering its **250th C-130J tail assembly**, also known as the **empennage**.
 
• **TLMAL** is a **joint venture** between **Tata Advanced Systems Limited (TASL)** and the **US-based** global security and aerospace leader **Lockheed Martin**, which was established in **2010**.
 
• The **TLMAL** facility, located in **Adibatla, Hyderabad**, serves as the **sole global production source** for **C-130J empennage** assemblies, which are integrated into all **Super Hercules** aircraft produced in the **United States**.
 
• The **empennage** consists of the aircraft's entire tail section, including the **horizontal and vertical stabilizers**, as well as the **leading edges** and **tip assemblies**.
 
• This milestone reflects the maturity of the **Indian** aerospace ecosystem and the success of the **Make in India** initiative, as these locally manufactured components support a global fleet operated by **22 nations**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **C-130J Super Hercules:**
 
 
• The **C-130J Super Hercules** is the world’s most advanced tactical airlifter, known for its versatility in combat, humanitarian aid, and disaster relief missions.
 
• The **Indian Air Force (IAF)** operates a fleet of **C-130J-30s**, which are used for special operations and transport in challenging terrains.
 
 
 
• **Tata Advanced Systems Limited (TASL):**
 
 
• **TASL** is the strategic aerospace and defense arm of the **Tata Group** and is a key player in **India's** mission to become self-reliant in defense manufacturing (**Atmanirbhar Bharat**).
 
• Beyond the **C-130J** project, **TASL** is involved in several other high-profile aerospace projects, including the **C-295** transport aircraft manufacturing program.
 
 
 
• **Growth and Export Impact:**
 
 
• The **TLMAL** joint venture has a high export orientation, with over **90%** of its manufactured components being sent to **Lockheed Martin’s** final assembly line in **Marietta, Georgia**.
 
• The facility reached the delivery of its **100th empennage** in **2018** and its **150th** in **September 2021**, indicating a steady increase in production efficiency over the years.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **TLMAL** facility also hosts a specialized **Metal-to-Metal Bonding** facility, which was added in **2018** to enhance its technological capabilities and local content.
 
• This **joint venture** serves as a model for private sector participation in **Indian** defense, showcasing how **global original equipment manufacturers (OEMs)** can partner with **Indian** firms to create a robust domestic supply chain.
 
• By **December 2025**, the total number of **C-130J** aircraft delivered globally has expanded significantly, all featuring the critical tail assemblies manufactured in **Hyderabad**.
